name: Start
description: Windows MDM settings in the Start category, applied as OMA-URI (SyncML) values.

properties.name: Allow Pinned Folder Documents
properties.description: This policy controls the visibility of the Documents shortcut on the Start menu. The possible values are 0 - means that the shortcut should be hidden and grays out the corresponding toggle in the Settings app, 1 - means that the shortcut should be visible and grays out the corresponding toggle in the Settings app, 65535 - means that there is no enforced configuration and the setting can be changed by the user.

enum.description: The shortcut is hidden and disables the setting in the Settings app.
The shortcut is visible and disables the setting in the Settings app.
There is no enforced configuration and the setting can be changed by the user.

properties.name: Configure Start Pins
properties.description: Allows admin to override the default items pinned to Start.

properties.name: Configure Start Pins (User)
properties.description: Allows admin to override the default items pinned to Start.

properties.name: Disable Context Menus
properties.description: Enabling this policy prevents context menus from being invoked in the Start Menu.

properties.name: Disable Context Menus (User)
properties.description: Enabling this policy prevents context menus from being invoked in the Start Menu.

properties.name: Disable Editing Quick Settings
properties.description: Allows admin to disable editing Quick Settings, such as by accessing the 'Edit quick settings' context through right-clicking on Quick Settings buttons.

properties.name: Force Start Size
properties.description: Forces the start screen size. If there is policy configuration conflict, the latest configuration request is applied to the device.

enum.description: Do not force size of Start.
Force a fullscreen size of Start.

properties.name: Force Start Size (User)
properties.description: Forces the start screen size. If there is policy configuration conflict, the latest configuration request is applied to the device.

enum.description: Do not force size of Start.
Force a fullscreen size of Start.

properties.name: Hide App List
properties.description: Setting the value of this policy to 1 or 2 collapses the app list. Setting the value of this policy to 3 removes the app list entirely. Setting the value of this policy to 2 or 3 disables the corresponding toggle in the Settings app.

enum.description: Hide all apps list, and Disable "Show app list in Start menu" in Settings app.
Hide all apps list, remove all apps button, and Disable "Show app list in Start menu" in Settings app.

properties.name: Hide App List (User)
properties.description: Setting the value of this policy to 1 or 2 collapses the app list. Setting the value of this policy to 3 removes the app list entirely. Setting the value of this policy to 2 or 3 disables the corresponding toggle in the Settings app.

enum.description: Hide all apps list, and Disable "Show app list in Start menu" in Settings app.

properties.name: Hide Category View
properties.description: This policy setting allows you to hide the category view in the Start Menu. If you enable this policy setting, the Start Menu will no longer show the category view as an option and will default to grid view.

properties.name: Hide Category View (User)
properties.description: This policy setting allows you to hide the category view in the Start Menu. If you enable this policy setting, the Start Menu will no longer show the category view as an option and will default to grid view.

properties.name: Hide Change Account Settings
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides "Change account settings" from appearing in the user tile in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide Frequently Used Apps
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides the most used apps from appearing on the start menu and disables the corresponding toggle in the Settings app.

properties.name: Hide Frequently Used Apps (User)
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides the most used apps from appearing on the start menu and disables the corresponding toggle in the Settings app.

properties.name: Hide Hibernate
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides "Hibernate" from appearing in the power button in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide Lock
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides "Lock" from appearing in the user tile in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide People Bar (User)
properties.description: Enabling this policy removes the people icon from the taskbar as well as the corresponding settings toggle. It also prevents users from pinning people to the taskbar.

properties.name: Hide Power Button
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides the power button from appearing in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide Recent Jumplists
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides recent jumplists from appearing on the start menu/taskbar and disables the corresponding toggle in the Settings app.

properties.name: Hide Recent Jumplists (User)
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides recent jumplists from appearing on the start menu/taskbar and disables the corresponding toggle in the Settings app.

properties.name: Hide Recently Added Apps
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides recently added apps from appearing on the start menu and disables the corresponding toggle in the Settings app.

properties.name: Hide Recently Added Apps (User)
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides recently added apps from appearing on the start menu and disables the corresponding toggle in the Settings app.

properties.name: Hide Restart
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides "Restart/Update and restart" from appearing in the power button in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide Shut Down
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides "Shut down/Update and shut down" from appearing in the power button in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide Sign Out
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides "Sign out" from appearing in the user tile in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide Sleep
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides "Sleep" from appearing in the power button in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide Switch Account
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides "Switch account" from appearing in the user tile in the start menu.

properties.name: Hide User Tile
properties.description: Enabling this policy hides the user tile from appearing in the start menu.

properties.name: Import Edge Assets
properties.description: This policy setting allows you to import Edge assets to be used with StartLayout policy. Start layout can contain secondary tile from Edge app which looks for Edge local asset file. Edge local asset would not exist and cause Edge secondary tile to appear empty in this case. This policy only gets applied when StartLayout policy is modified.

properties.name: No Pinning To Taskbar
properties.description: This policy setting allows you to control pinning programs to the Taskbar. If you enable this policy setting, users cannot change the programs currently pinned to the Taskbar. If any programs are already pinned to the Taskbar, these programs continue to show in the Taskbar. However, users cannot unpin these programs already pinned to the Taskbar, and they cannot pin new programs to the Taskbar. If you disable or do not configure this policy setting, users can change the programs currently pinned to the Taskbar.

properties.name: Simplify Quick Settings
properties.description: Allows admin to control the Quick Settings layout. If enabled, fewer Quick Settings buttons will be shown (only WiFi, Bluetooth, VPN, and Accessibility). If disabled or not configured, the regular Quick Settings layout will be loaded.

properties.name: Start Layout
properties.description: Important For more information, see Policy scope. Allows you to override the default Start layout and prevents the user from changing it. If both user and device policies are set, the user policy will be used. Apps pinned to the taskbar can also be changed with this policyFor further details on how to customize the Start layout, please see Customize and export Start layout and Configure Windows 10 taskbar.

properties.name: Start Layout (User)
properties.description: Important For more information, see Policy scope. Allows you to override the default Start layout and prevents the user from changing it. If both user and device policies are set, the user policy will be used. Apps pinned to the taskbar can also be changed with this policyFor further details on how to customize the Start layout, please see Customize and export Start layout and Configure Windows 10 taskbar.
